docs.text: Hello world IXWebSocket is a C++ library for WebSocket client and server development. It has minimal dependencies (no boost), is very simple to use and support everything you'll likely need for websocket dev (SSL, deflate compression, compiles on most platforms, etc...). HTTP client and server code is also available, but it hasn't received as much testing. It is been used on big mobile video game titles sending and receiving tons of messages since 2017 (iOS and Android). It was tested on macOS, iOS, Linux, Android, Windows and FreeBSD. Note that the MinGW compiler is not supported at this point. Two important design goals are simplicity and correctness. A bad security bug affecting users compiling with SSL enabled and OpenSSL as the backend was just fixed in newly released version 11.0.0. Please upgrade ! (more details in the https://github.com/machinezone/IXWebSocket/pull/250 . /* * main.cpp * Author: Benjamin Sergeant * Copyright (c) 2020 Machine Zone, Inc. All rights reserved. * * Super simple standalone example. See ws folder, unittest and doc/usage.md for more. * * On macOS * $ mkdir -p build ; (cd build ; cmake -DUSE_TLS=1 .. ; make -j ; make install) * $ clang++ --std=c++11 --stdlib=libc++ main.cpp -lixwebsocket -lz -framework Security -framework Foundation * $ ./a.out * * Or use cmake -DBUILD_DEMO=ON option for other platforms */ #include <ixwebsocket/IXNetSystem.h> #include <ixwebsocket/IXWebSocket.h> #include <ixwebsocket/IXUserAgent.h> #include <iostream> int main() { // Required on Windows ix::initNetSystem(); // Our websocket object ix::WebSocket webSocket; // Connect to a server with encryption // See https://machinezone.github.io/IXWebSocket/usage/#tls-support-and-configuration std::string url("wss://echo.websocket.org"); webSocket.setUrl(url); std::cout << "Connecting to " << url << "..." << std::endl; // Setup a callback to be fired (in a background thread, watch out for race conditions !) // when a message or an event (open, close, error) is received webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Message) { std::cout << "received message: " << msg->str << std::endl; std::cout << "> " << std::flush; } else if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Open) { std::cout << "Connection established" << std::endl; std::cout << "> " << std::flush; } else if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Error) { // Maybe SSL is not configured properly std::cout << "Connection error: " << msg->errorInfo.reason << std::endl; std::cout << "> " << std::flush; } } ); // Now that our callback is setup, we can start our background thread and receive messages webSocket.start(); // Send a message to the server (default to TEXT mode) webSocket.send("hello world"); // Display a prompt std::cout << "> " << std::flush; std::string text; // Read text from the console and send messages in text mode. // Exit with Ctrl-D on Unix or Ctrl-Z on Windows. while (std::getline(std::cin, text)) { webSocket.send(text); std::cout << "> " << std::flush; } return 0; } Interested? Go read the docs ! If things don't work as expected, please create an issue on GitHub, or even better a pull request if you know how to fix your problem. IXWebSocket is actively being developed, check out the changelog to know what's cooking. If you are looking for a real time messaging service (the chat-like 'server' your websocket code will talk to) with many features such as history, backed by Redis, look at cobra . IXWebSocket client code is autobahn compliant beginning with the 6.0.0 version. See the current test results . Some tests are still failing in the server code. Starting with the 11.0.8 release, IXWebSocket should be fully C++11 compatible. Users If your company or project is using this library, feel free to open an issue or PR to amend this list. Machine Zone Tokio , a discord library focused on audio playback with node bindings. libDiscordBot , an easy to use Discord-bot framework. gwebsocket , a websocket (lua) module for Garry's Mod DisCPP , a simple but feature rich Discord API wrapper discord.cpp , a discord library for making bots Teleport , Teleport is your own personal remote robot avatar Alternative libraries There are plenty of great websocket libraries out there, which might work for you. Here are a couple of serious ones. websocketpp - C++ beast - C++ libwebsockets - C µWebSockets - C wslay - C uvweb is a library written by the IXWebSocket author which is built on top of uvw , which is a C++ wrapper for libuv . It has more dependencies and does not support SSL at this point, but it can be used to open multiple connections within a single OS thread thanks to libuv. To check the performance of a websocket library, you can look at the autoroute project. docs.text: Changelog All changes to this project will be documented in this file. [13.0.0] - 2026-11-20 — Enguerrand de Marigny This major release collects 53 merged pull requests since v12.1.0, with improvements to WebSocket closure and reconnection, TLS backends, HTTP streaming and connection reuse, proxy support, packaging, and compliance testing. Highlights and upgrade notes HTTP uploads can stream known-length bodies through onUploadCallback , or unknown-length bodies using Transfer-Encoding: chunked . HTTP clients reuse eligible persistent connections, and an authenticated idle HTTP connection can be explicitly handed to WebSocket. Normal WebSocket start() keeps its existing connection model. HTTP and WebSocket servers support host/port configuration after construction, retries after failed binds, and OS-assigned ports. The HTTP server has a configurable document root. Add an opt-in incoming WebSocket message limit; the default remains unlimited. Add TLS certificate/key loading from memory and optional OpenSSL TLS key logging. Harden close/reconnect ordering, send queues, DNS worker lifetime, redirect credential handling, HTTP framing, gzip completeness checks, and TLS error reporting. Add shared SOCKS5 support to HTTP/WebSocket clients and proxy options to ws . Fix installed-package integration for compression: generated public codec configuration makes direct-include and pkg-config consumers use the library's layout; CMake discovers Threads; static pkg-config metadata includes zlib only when compression is enabled. Install the generated IXWebSocketCodecConfig.h with the other public headers. Add Autobahn compliance CI, local interactive progress reporting, and a standalone ws bench command. The proposed reference-callback API from #536 is not included. C++11 remains the library minimum. Rebuild applications and dependent libraries against this major release; the CMake project/runtime version is 13.0.0 and shared-library SOVERSION is 13. Complete change list WebSocket and connection handling Add shared SOCKS5 support to WebSocket and HTTP clients ( PR #580 ). Accept LF-only HTTP headers with simpler bounded parsing ( PR #616 ). Discard stale WebSocket state when reconnecting ( PR #617 ; resolves #610 , #611 ). Stop WebSocket message callbacks after closing begins ( PR #620 ). End server handshake error responses and answer 426 for other versions ( PR #624 ). Prevent WebSocket busy loops after socket poll failures ( PR #626 ; resolves #623 ). Add setDisabledDefaultHeaders for optional handshake headers ( PR #627 ). Fix Autobahn compliance while preserving close lifecycle guarantees ( PR #629 ). Prevent concurrent close from reopening a closed transport ( PR #633 ; resolves #632 ). Fix send-failure callbacks racing message delivery ( PR #635 ; resolves #551 ). Expose rejected handshake response headers in Error events ( PR #637 ; resolves #636 ). Make protocol case comparisons independent of locale ( PR #640 ; resolves #398 ). Remove trailing newlines from WebSocket handshake errors ( PR #641 ; resolves #463 ). Fix proxy connection-state leak and upstream cleanup ( PR #642 ; resolves #490 ). Preserve socket errors in connection failure diagnostics ( PR #645 ). Stop socket reads at EOF or the requested byte count ( PR #649 ). Fix DNS worker lifetime and add a synchronous resolver fallback ( PR #656 ; resolves #364 ). Keep HTTP and WebSocket redirect credentials within the same origin ( PR #658 ). Add opt-in incoming WebSocket message size limits ( PR #662 ). HTTP and server APIs Preserve asynchronous HTTP request configuration when queued ( PR #643 ). Fix URL encoding and concurrent multipart boundary generation ( PR #646 ). Fix HTTP response framing, redirects and streamed byte counts ( PR #647 ). Preserve static file bytes and ignore URI queries ( PR #648 ). Fix URL fragments, empty queries and locale-dependent validation ( PR #651 ). Reject truncated gzip streams instead of returning partial success ( PR #652 ). Validate HTTP request lengths and emit one response length ( PR #653 ). Add a configurable document root to the HTTP server ( PR #659 ; resolves #447 ). Stream HTTP request bodies for large file uploads ( PR #663 ; resolves #556 ). Reuse persistent HTTP client connections ( PR #665 ; resolves #484 ). Upgrade authenticated HTTP connections to WebSocket ( PR #666 ; resolves #434 ). Support chunked HTTP request uploads ( PR #668 ; resolves #381 ). Allow configuring server host and port before listening ( PR #669 ; resolves #470 ). TLS and security backends Keep server TLS handshakes off the accept loop ( PR #618 ). fix(tls): preserve pending writes in the shared send queue ( PR #619 ). Fix OpenSSL builds with deprecated APIs disabled ( PR #634 ; resolves #518 ). Explain unsupported system CA loading with Mbed TLS ( PR #644 ; resolves #526 ). Report TLS EOF and terminal errors consistently across backends ( PR #650 ). Avoid busy-spinning during TLS client handshakes ( PR #655 ; resolves #525 ). Close SecureTransport native sockets without a TLS context ( PR #657 ). Add opt-in OpenSSL TLS key logging for clients and servers ( PR #661 ; resolves #499 ). Load TLS certificate chains and private keys from memory ( PR #664 ; resolves #533 ). Build, packaging, and portability Respect caller CMake settings while retaining the C++11 minimum ( PR #465 ). Enable shadow warnings and optional warnings-as-errors (#531) ( PR #535 ; resolves #531 ). Link libatomic when required for 64-bit atomics ( PR #621 ; resolves #513 ). Fix Windows DLL imports without breaking static MinGW builds ( PR #631 ; resolves #602 ). Require braces and enforce clang-format in CI ( PR #660 ). Fix installed compression layout and package dependencies ( PR #670 ). Tools, compliance, and documentation Add opt-in Docker Autobahn compliance check ( PR #628 ). Add interactive reporting for local Autobahn runs ( PR #630 ). Document WebSocket callback threads and shutdown ownership ( PR #638 ; resolves #457 ). Add SOCKS5 proxy options to ws connect and curl ( PR #639 ). Clarify connection handles, parallel starts and TLS listener setup ( PR #654 ). Add a self-contained ws bench command ( PR #667 ). docs.text: HTTP uploads can stream known-length bodies through onUploadCallback , or unknown-length bodies using Transfer-Encoding: chunked . HTTP clients reuse eligible persistent connections, and an authenticated idle HTTP connection can be explicitly handed to WebSocket. Normal WebSocket start() keeps its existing connection model. HTTP and WebSocket servers support host/port configuration after construction, retries after failed binds, and OS-assigned ports. The HTTP server has a configurable document root. Add an opt-in incoming WebSocket message limit; the default remains unlimited. Add TLS certificate/key loading from memory and optional OpenSSL TLS key logging. Harden close/reconnect ordering, send queues, DNS worker lifetime, redirect credential handling, HTTP framing, gzip completeness checks, and TLS error reporting. Add shared SOCKS5 support to HTTP/WebSocket clients and proxy options to ws . Fix installed-package integration for compression: generated public codec configuration makes direct-include and pkg-config consumers use the library's layout; CMake discovers Threads; static pkg-config metadata includes zlib only when compression is enabled. Install the generated IXWebSocketCodecConfig.h with the other public headers. Add Autobahn compliance CI, local interactive progress reporting, and a standalone ws bench command. The proposed reference-callback API from #536 is not included. C++11 remains the library minimum. Rebuild applications and dependent libraries against this major release; the CMake project/runtime version is 13.0.0 and shared-library SOVERSION is 13.

docs.text: Add shared SOCKS5 support to WebSocket and HTTP clients ( PR #580 ). Accept LF-only HTTP headers with simpler bounded parsing ( PR #616 ). Discard stale WebSocket state when reconnecting ( PR #617 ; resolves #610 , #611 ). Stop WebSocket message callbacks after closing begins ( PR #620 ). End server handshake error responses and answer 426 for other versions ( PR #624 ). Prevent WebSocket busy loops after socket poll failures ( PR #626 ; resolves #623 ). Add setDisabledDefaultHeaders for optional handshake headers ( PR #627 ). Fix Autobahn compliance while preserving close lifecycle guarantees ( PR #629 ). Prevent concurrent close from reopening a closed transport ( PR #633 ; resolves #632 ). Fix send-failure callbacks racing message delivery ( PR #635 ; resolves #551 ). Expose rejected handshake response headers in Error events ( PR #637 ; resolves #636 ). Make protocol case comparisons independent of locale ( PR #640 ; resolves #398 ). Remove trailing newlines from WebSocket handshake errors ( PR #641 ; resolves #463 ). Fix proxy connection-state leak and upstream cleanup ( PR #642 ; resolves #490 ). Preserve socket errors in connection failure diagnostics ( PR #645 ). Stop socket reads at EOF or the requested byte count ( PR #649 ). Fix DNS worker lifetime and add a synchronous resolver fallback ( PR #656 ; resolves #364 ). Keep HTTP and WebSocket redirect credentials within the same origin ( PR #658 ). Add opt-in incoming WebSocket message size limits ( PR #662 ).
docs.title: WebSocket and connection handling

docs.text: Preserve asynchronous HTTP request configuration when queued ( PR #643 ). Fix URL encoding and concurrent multipart boundary generation ( PR #646 ). Fix HTTP response framing, redirects and streamed byte counts ( PR #647 ). Preserve static file bytes and ignore URI queries ( PR #648 ). Fix URL fragments, empty queries and locale-dependent validation ( PR #651 ). Reject truncated gzip streams instead of returning partial success ( PR #652 ). Validate HTTP request lengths and emit one response length ( PR #653 ). Add a configurable document root to the HTTP server ( PR #659 ; resolves #447 ). Stream HTTP request bodies for large file uploads ( PR #663 ; resolves #556 ). Reuse persistent HTTP client connections ( PR #665 ; resolves #484 ). Upgrade authenticated HTTP connections to WebSocket ( PR #666 ; resolves #434 ). Support chunked HTTP request uploads ( PR #668 ; resolves #381 ). Allow configuring server host and port before listening ( PR #669 ; resolves #470 ).

docs.text: Keep server TLS handshakes off the accept loop ( PR #618 ). fix(tls): preserve pending writes in the shared send queue ( PR #619 ). Fix OpenSSL builds with deprecated APIs disabled ( PR #634 ; resolves #518 ). Explain unsupported system CA loading with Mbed TLS ( PR #644 ; resolves #526 ). Report TLS EOF and terminal errors consistently across backends ( PR #650 ). Avoid busy-spinning during TLS client handshakes ( PR #655 ; resolves #525 ). Close SecureTransport native sockets without a TLS context ( PR #657 ). Add opt-in OpenSSL TLS key logging for clients and servers ( PR #661 ; resolves #499 ). Load TLS certificate chains and private keys from memory ( PR #664 ; resolves #533 ).
docs.title: TLS and security backends

docs.text: Respect caller CMake settings while retaining the C++11 minimum ( PR #465 ). Enable shadow warnings and optional warnings-as-errors (#531) ( PR #535 ; resolves #531 ). Link libatomic when required for 64-bit atomics ( PR #621 ; resolves #513 ). Fix Windows DLL imports without breaking static MinGW builds ( PR #631 ; resolves #602 ). Clarify connection handles, parallel starts and TLS listener setup ( PR #654 ). Add a self-contained ws bench command ( PR #667 ).

docs.text: Add an opt-in native macOS Network.framework TLS backend for HTTP/WebSocket clients and servers, including TLS 1.3, mutual TLS, and Apple certificate trust evaluation, without linking OpenSSL (#615). Fix a WebSocket shutdown race that could trigger an automatic reconnect and block stop() indefinitely (#609). Prevent path traversal in the HTTP server's default file handler (#608). Fix mbedTLS TLS 1.3 reads and Windows errno signaling (#594), and keep PSA crypto initialized until network-system teardown (#613). Add server error logging callbacks for failures before a WebSocket connection exists (#595). Add close-on-exec support for server and accepted sockets (#604). Allow omitting client/server window-bit parameters from per-message deflate offers (#599). Remove CMake FetchContent downloads; developer tools and tests use vendored dependencies (#605). Set the shared-library soversion (#607), improve MSVC type compatibility (#597), and fix build warnings (#572). Align the runtime and CMake version numbers. Release notes

docs.text: Autobahn compliance The autobahn GitHub Actions workflow tests the WebSocket client and echo server using Docker. Add the autobahn label to a pull request to run it. New commits rerun the check while the label remains; removing the label skips it. It also runs on merges to master and can be started manually from the Actions tab, including against a release branch or tag. The workflow calls one make target: make -f makefile.dev test_autobahn For a live local progress display, run: make -f makefile.dev test_autobahn_interactive The display shows the current case ID, cases started, and elapsed time for each role, followed by a validated PASS/FAIL summary and the report directory. Case progress is not a pass count: results are checked after each role finishes. A terminal updates one line in place; redirected output uses plain progress lines. Ctrl-C stops the run and cleans up its containers. To select a smaller run through make: make -f makefile.dev test_autobahn_interactive AUTOBAHN_ARGS="--cases 6.4.* --role client" Docker and Python 3 are required. The library is built from the current checkout with C++11 and zlib enabled. This checks WebSocket framing, closing, UTF-8, and compression in both directions over plain WebSocket connections; it does not test TLS backends. The pinned Autobahn image is amd64, so Docker Desktop uses emulation on Apple Silicon. Both roles run every case in the pinned suite, without exclusions. The runner checks the exact case IDs against a manifest generated by that suite, then checks both behavior and behaviorClose . Only OK and INFORMATIONAL pass; missing cases, malformed reports, unknown statuses, non-strict results, and closing failures fail the check. Process success alone is insufficient. Reports are recreated under build/autobahn/reports/client and build/autobahn/reports/server . Open each index.html for detailed results. Container logs and the selected suite/image IDs are also saved under build/autobahn . CI uploads these as the autobahn-reports artifact even when tests fail. Each role has a 30-minute limit; the whole CI job has a 75-minute limit including the build. For a faster local investigation, select cases or a role: python3 tools/run_autobahn.py --role client --cases '1.*,2.*' --output build/autobahn-debug CI always uses the full case selection. Generated containers and their private Docker network are removed after the run. A lock prevents simultaneous runs from overwriting the same output directory. To block merging labelled PRs on compliance failures, make the autobahn check required in the repository's branch protection or ruleset. Unlabelled PRs skip that job, which GitHub treats as successful even for a required check. A failure on master happens after merging and cannot prevent that merge. See GitHub's job condition documentation .

docs.text: Build Building static libraries A static library can be build using: mkdir build #make a build dir so that you can build out of tree cd build cmake -DUSE_TLS=1 .. make -j There are also two build scripts in the tools folder for creating static libraries for android and iOS/macOS respectively. Arguments can be changed in the script files. Android: mkdir build cd build ./../tools/build_android.sh make -j macOS & iOS: mkdir build cd build ./../tools/build_ios.sh CMake CMakefiles for the library and the examples are available. This library has few dependencies, so it is possible to just add the source files into your project. docs.text: Implementation details Per Message Deflate compression. The per message deflate compression option is supported. It can lead to very nice bandbwith savings (20x !) if your messages are similar, which is often the case for example for chat applications. All features of the spec should be supported. TLS/SSL Connections can be optionally secured and encrypted with TLS/SSL when using a wss:// endpoint, or using normal un-encrypted socket with ws:// endpoints. AppleSSL is used on iOS and macOS, OpenSSL and mbedTLS can be used on Android, Linux and Windows. If you are using OpenSSL, try to be on a version higher than 1.1.x as there there are thread safety problems with 1.0.x. Polling and background thread work For callback execution contexts, synchronous connection mode, and shutdown guidance, see Threading and callbacks . No manual polling to fetch data is required. Data is sent and received instantly by using a background thread for receiving data and the select system call to be notified by the OS of incoming data. No timeout is used for select so that the background thread is only woken up when data is available, to optimize battery life. This is also the recommended way of using select according to the select tutorial, section select law . Read and Writes to the socket are non blocking. Data is sent right away and not enqueued by writing directly to the socket, which is possible since system socket implementations allow concurrent read/writes. Automatic reconnection If the remote end (server) breaks the connection, the code will try to perpetually reconnect, by using an exponential backoff strategy, capped at one retry every 10 seconds. This behavior can be disabled. Large messages Large frames are broken up into smaller chunks or messages to avoid filling up the os tcp buffers, which is permitted thanks to WebSocket fragmentation . Messages up to 1G were sent and received succesfully. Testing The library has an interactive tool which is handy for testing compatibility ith other libraries. We have tested our client against Python, Erlang, Node.js, and C++ websocket server libraries. The unittest tries to be comprehensive, and has been running on multiple platforms, with different sanitizers such as a thread sanitizer to catch data races or the undefined behavior sanitizer. The regression test is running after each commit on github actions for multiple configurations. Limitations On some configuration (mostly Android) certificate validation needs to be setup so that SocketTLSOptions.caFile point to a pem file, such as the one distributed by Firefox. Unless that setup is done connecting to a wss endpoint will display an error. With mbedtls the message will contain error in handshake : X509 - Certificate verification failed, e.g. CRL, CA or signature check failed . Automatic reconnection works at the TCP socket level, and will detect remote end disconnects. However, if the device/computer network become unreachable (by turning off wifi), it is quite hard to reliably and timely detect it at the socket level using recv and send error codes. Here is a good discussion on the subject. This behavior is consistent with other runtimes such as node.js. One way to detect a disconnected device with low level C code is to do a name resolution with DNS but this can be expensive. Mobile devices have good and reliable API to do that. The server code is using select to detect incoming data, and creates one OS thread per connection. This is not as scalable as strategies using epoll or kqueue. C++ code organization Here is a simplistic diagram which explains how the code is structured in term of class/modules. +-----------------------+ --- Public | | Start the receiving Background thread. Auto reconnection. Simple websocket Ping. | IXWebSocket | Interface used by C++ test clients. No IX dependencies. | | +-----------------------+ | | | IXWebSocketServer | Run a server and give each connections its own WebSocket object. | | Each connection is handled in a new OS thread. | | +-----------------------+ --- Private | | | IXWebSocketTransport | Low level websocket code, framing, managing raw socket. Adapted from easywsclient. | | +-----------------------+ | | | IXWebSocketHandshake | Establish the connection between client and server. | | +-----------------------+ | | | IXWebSocket | ws:// Unencrypted Socket handler | IXWebSocketAppleSSL | wss:// TLS encrypted Socket AppleSSL handler. Used on iOS and macOS | IXWebSocketOpenSSL | wss:// TLS encrypted Socket OpenSSL handler. Used on Android and Linux | | Can be used on macOS too. +-----------------------+ | | | IXSocketConnect | Connect to the remote host (client). | | +-----------------------+ | | | IXDNSLookup | Does DNS resolution asynchronously so that it can be interrupted. | | +-----------------------+

docs.text: Examples The ws folder countains many interactive programs for chat, file transfers , curl like http clients, demonstrating client and server usage. Windows note To use the network system on Windows, you need to initialize it once with WSAStartup() and clean it up with WSACleanup() . We have helpers for that which you can use, see below. This init would typically take place in your main function. On every platform, ix::uninitNetSystem() also releases process-global TLS state (mbedTLS PSA crypto, with mbedTLS >= 3.6), so call it only after all sockets are closed. #include <ixwebsocket/IXNetSystem.h> int main() { ix::initNetSystem(); ... ix::uninitNetSystem(); return 0; } WebSocket client API #include <ixwebsocket/IXWebSocket.h> ... // Our websocket object ix::WebSocket webSocket; std::string url("ws://localhost:8080/"); webSocket.setUrl(url); // Optional heart beat, sent every 45 seconds when there is not any traffic // to make sure that load balancers do not kill an idle connection. webSocket.setPingInterval(45); // Per message deflate connection is not enabled by default. You can tweak its parameters, enable or disable it with webSocket.enablePerMessageDeflate(); webSocket.disablePerMessageDeflate(); // Setup a callback to be fired when a message or an event (open, close, error) is received webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Message) { std::cout << msg->str << std::endl; } } ); // Now that our callback is setup, we can start our background thread and receive messages webSocket.start(); // Send a message to the server (default to TEXT mode) webSocket.send("hello world"); // The message can be sent in BINARY mode (useful if you send MsgPack data for example) webSocket.sendBinary("some serialized binary data"); // ... finally ... // Stop the connection webSocket.stop() Sending messages WebSocketSendInfo result = websocket.send("foo") will send a message. If the connection was closed, sending will fail, and the success field of the result object will be set to false. There could also be a compression error in which case the compressError field will be set to true. The payloadSize field and wireSize fields will tell you respectively how much bytes the message weight, and how many bytes were sent on the wire (potentially compressed + counting the message header (a few bytes). There is an optional progress callback that can be passed in as the second argument. If a message is large it will be fragmented into chunks which will be sent independantly. Everytime the we can write a fragment into the OS network cache, the callback will be invoked. If a user wants to cancel a slow send, false should be returned from within the callback. Here is an example code snippet copied from the ws send sub-command. Each fragment weights 32K, so the total integer is the wireSize divided by 32K. As an example if you are sending 32M of data, uncompressed, total will be 1000. current will be set to 0 for the first fragment, then 1, 2 etc... auto result = _webSocket.sendBinary(serializedMsg, [this, throttle](int current, int total) -> bool { ix::logInfo("ws_send: Step {} out of {}", current + 1, total); if (throttle) { std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli> duration(10); std::this_thread::sleep_for(duration); } return _connected; }); The send() and sendText() methods check that the string contains only valid UTF-8 characters. If you know that the string is a valid UTF-8 string you can skip that step and use the sendUtf8Text method instead. With the IXWebSocketSendData overloads of sendUtf8Text and sendBinary it is possible to not only send std::string but also std::vector<char> , std::vector<uint8_t> and char* . std::vector<uint8_t> data({1, 2, 3, 4}); auto result = webSocket.sendBinary(data); const char* text = "Hello World!"; result = webSocket.sendUtf8Text(IXWebSocketSendData(text, strlen(text))); Incoming message size limit Incoming messages are unlimited by default. Set a limit in bytes before connecting or starting the server: webSocket.setMaxMessageSize(1024 * 1024); // Client: 1 MiB per incoming message. server.setMaxMessageSize(1024 * 1024); // Server: default for new connections. getMaxMessageSize() returns the configured limit; setMaxMessageSize(0) restores unlimited messages. Client settings apply on the next connection, including reconnections. Server settings also apply to WebSocket upgrades through HttpServer . The limit covers the combined payload of all fragments, both before and after per-message decompression. Control frames do not count toward the limit. Oversized messages close the connection with code 1009 (Message Too Big), without delivering that message. Frame lengths are checked before buffering their payload; decompression stops before appending output beyond the limit. This is a per-message limit, rather than a total process memory budget. Choose it alongside your connection limit and application buffering requirements. The echo server exposes the same setting: ws echo_server --port 8080 --max-message-size 1048576 ReadyState getReadyState() returns the state of the connection. There are 4 possible states. ReadyState::Connecting - The connection is not yet open. ReadyState::Open - The connection is open and ready to communicate. ReadyState::Closing - The connection is in the process of closing. ReadyState::Closed - The connection is closed or could not be opened. Open and Close notifications The onMessage event will be fired when the connection is opened or closed. This is similar to the JavaScript browser API , which has open and close events notification that can be registered with the browser addEventListener . webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Open) { std::cout << "send greetings" << std::endl; // Headers can be inspected (pairs of string/string) std::cout << "Handshake Headers:" << std::endl; for (auto it : msg->headers) { std::cout << it.first << ": " << it.second << std::endl; } } else if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Close) { std::cout << "disconnected" << std::endl; // The server can send an explicit code and reason for closing. // This data can be accessed through the closeInfo object. std::cout << msg->closeInfo.code << std::endl; std::cout << msg->closeInfo.reason << std::endl; } } ); Error notification A message will be fired when there is an error with the connection. The message type will be ix::WebSocketMessageType::Error . Multiple fields will be available on the event to describe the error. When a server rejects the WebSocket handshake, msg->errorInfo.headers contains the HTTP response headers, such as Retry-After or custom authentication headers. Header names are case insensitive. Errors without response headers leave this map empty. webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Error) { std::stringstream ss; ss << "Error: " << msg->errorInfo.reason << std::endl; ss << "#retries: " << msg->errorInfo.retries << std::endl; ss << "Wait time(ms): " << msg->errorInfo.wait_time << std::endl; ss << "HTTP Status: " << msg->errorInfo.http_status << std::endl; std::cout << ss.str() << std::endl; } } ); start, stop websocket.start() starts a background thread that connects to the remote server and processes incoming events. websocket.stop() requests closure and waits for that background thread to exit. For parallel connections, configure a separate ix::WebSocket for each URL and call start() on each instance. Each connection attempt runs on its own background thread, so starting another client does not wait for the first handshake. connect() is the synchronous connection API. Threading and callbacks setOnMessageCallback() handles Open, Message, Close, Error, Ping, Pong, and Fragment events. Callbacks execute inline on the thread processing the connection; they are not dispatched to an application event loop or the main thread. Connection mode Thread executing event callbacks Client using start() The client's background connection thread, including connection attempts and automatic reconnections. Client calling connect() explicitly A successful connection invokes Open on the thread calling connect() . A failed connection is returned as a WebSocketInitResult . Client calling run() explicitly The thread calling run() processes subsequent events. Call connect() first, and do not combine this mode with start() . WebSocketServer Each connection has its own worker thread. The connection setup callback and that connection's event callbacks run on this thread. Different connections can invoke application callbacks concurrently. For a connection owned by start() or WebSocketServer , message events and the terminal Close notification are processed on its connection thread. A fatal socket write failure makes send() return an unsuccessful WebSocketSendInfo and request closure without invoking the message handler on the sending thread. The connection thread finishes any active message callback before delivering Close. Sending on an already closed connection also returns failure. Other callbacks have different execution contexts: Callback Execution thread Progress callback passed to send() The thread calling send() , during the send operation. Traffic tracker registered with setTrafficTrackerCallback() The sending thread for outgoing traffic and the connection thread for incoming traffic. This callback is shared across WebSocket instances and can be called concurrently. Keep event handlers short: a slow handler delays incoming messages, heartbeats, and close processing for that connection. To update a UI or perform lengthy work, copy the required data into an application queue and process it on the appropriate thread. Protect application state shared between callbacks and other threads. Register callbacks before starting the connection and leave them installed until processing has stopped. Do not replace a callback concurrently with its execution. Use only one owner to manage start() , stop() , and destruction; do not invoke these lifecycle operations concurrently. To disconnect from inside a message callback, call close() . Do not call stop() or destroy the WebSocket there: stop() joins the background thread created by start() , and server workers must return from their callbacks to finish shutdown. Call stop() from an owning application thread, and keep the WebSocket and any objects captured by its callbacks alive until processing has finished. Do not hold an application mutex across stop() if a callback needs that mutex, because stop() waits for the callback's thread to finish. Similarly, stop a server from outside its connection callbacks. Configuring the remote url The url can be set and queried after a websocket object has been created. You will have to call stop and start if you want to disconnect and connect to that new url. std::string url("wss://example.com"); websocket.configure(url); Ping/Pong support Ping/pong messages are used to implement keep-alive. 2 message types exists to identify ping and pong messages. Note that when a ping message is received, a pong is instantly send back as requested by the WebSocket spec. webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Ping || msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Pong) { std::cout << "pong data: " << msg->str << std::endl; } } ); A ping message can be sent to the server, with an optional data string. websocket.ping("ping data, optional (empty string is ok): limited to 125 bytes long"); Heartbeat. You can configure an optional heart beat / keep-alive, sent every 45 seconds when there is no any traffic to make sure that load balancers do not kill an idle connection. webSocket.setPingInterval(45); Supply extra HTTP headers. You can set extra HTTP headers to be sent during the WebSocket handshake. WebSocketHttpHeaders headers; headers["foo"] = "bar"; webSocket.setExtraHeaders(headers); To omit automatically generated User-Agent or Origin headers, set their names explicitly: webSocket.setDisabledDefaultHeaders({"User-Agent", "Origin"}); Names are case-insensitive. Only these optional defaults can be disabled; required handshake headers and other names are unaffected. Headers supplied through setExtraHeaders() always take precedence and are sent even when their values are empty. Pass an empty list to restore the defaults: webSocket.setDisabledDefaultHeaders({}); Changes apply to subsequent connections, including automatic reconnections. Subprotocols You can specify subprotocols to be set during the WebSocket handshake. For more info you can refer to this doc . webSocket.addSubprotocol("appProtocol-v1"); webSocket.addSubprotocol("appProtocol-v2"); The protocol that the server did accept is available in the open info protocol field. std::cout << "protocol: " << msg->openInfo.protocol << std::endl; Automatic reconnection Automatic reconnection kicks in when the connection is disconnected without the user consent. This feature is on by default and can be turned off. webSocket.enableAutomaticReconnection(); // turn on webSocket.disableAutomaticReconnection(); // turn off bool enabled = webSocket.isAutomaticReconnectionEnabled(); // query state The technique to calculate wait time is called exponential backoff . Here are the default waiting times between attempts (from connecting with ws connect ws://foo.com ) > Connection error: Got bad status connecting to foo.com, status: 301, HTTP Status line: HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently #retries: 1 Wait time(ms): 100 #retries: 2 Wait time(ms): 200 #retries: 3 Wait time(ms): 400 #retries: 4 Wait time(ms): 800 #retries: 5 Wait time(ms): 1600 #retries: 6 Wait time(ms): 3200 #retries: 7 Wait time(ms): 6400 #retries: 8 Wait time(ms): 10000 The waiting time is capped by default at 10s between 2 attempts, but that value can be changed and queried. The minimum waiting time can also be set. webSocket.setMaxWaitBetweenReconnectionRetries(5 * 1000); // 5000ms = 5s uint32_t m = webSocket.getMaxWaitBetweenReconnectionRetries(); webSocket.setMinWaitBetweenReconnectionRetries(1000); // 1000ms = 1s uint32_t m = webSocket.getMinWaitBetweenReconnectionRetries(); Handshake timeout You can control how long to wait until timing out while waiting for the websocket handshake to be performed. int handshakeTimeoutSecs = 1; setHandshakeTimeout(handshakeTimeoutSecs); WebSocket server API TLS handshakes run in individual connection workers, so an idle peer does not block other clients from connecting. Server TLS handshakes have a 10-second timeout and are cancelled when the server stops. The maximum connection limit includes clients whose TLS handshake is still pending. Configuring a server address after construction WebSocketServer and HttpServer also accept setHost() and setPort() before listen() . Construction does not bind a socket. Existing constructor arguments continue to work. ix::HttpServer server; server.setHost("0.0.0.0"); for (int port = 8080; port <= 8100; ++port) { server.setPort(port); auto result = server.listen(); if (result.first) { server.start(); break; } } A failed listen() leaves the instance available for another attempt. Once it succeeds, the setters and a second listen() return failure without changing the listener. Call stop() before reconfiguring and listening again. Invoke these configuration and lifecycle methods serially from the owning application thread. setHost() accepts the same numeric IPv4/IPv6 addresses as the constructor; the address is validated by listen() using the configured address family. setPort() rejects values outside 0–65535. To let the OS choose a free port, call setPort(0) ; after a successful listen() , getPort() returns the assigned port. Constructors also accept port zero. Connection setup callback setOnConnectionCallback() provides a std::weak_ptr<ix::WebSocket> and a ConnectionState for each accepted connection. Use this API when the application needs to retain a handle for later asynchronous sends. Register that connection's message callback inside the setup callback, as shown below. Use connectionState->getId() as the key in an application registry of weak pointers. Protect a registry shared by connection callbacks and application threads with a mutex. To send later, copy the weak pointer while holding the registry lock, release that lock, then call lock() on the weak pointer and send if it succeeds. An expired weak pointer cannot refer to a later connection, even if its allocation reuses the same address. Check the send result because the connection can close after lock() succeeds. Capturing a weak pointer also avoids a cycle between the WebSocket and its own callback. #include <ixwebsocket/IXWebSocketServer.h> ... // Run a server on localhost at a given port. // Bound host name, max connections and listen backlog can also be passed in as parameters. int port = 8008; std::string host("127.0.0.1"); // If you need this server to be accessible on a different machine, use "0.0.0.0" ix::WebSocketServer server(port, host); server.setOnConnectionCallback( [&server](std::weak_ptr<ix::WebSocket> webSocket, std::shared_ptr<ix::ConnectionState> connectionState) { std::cout << "Remote ip: " << connectionState->getRemoteIp() << std::endl; auto ws = webSocket.lock(); if (ws) { ws->setOnMessageCallback( [webSocket, connectionState, &server](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Open) { std::cout << "New connection" << std::endl; // A connection state object is available, and has a default id // You can subclass ConnectionState and pass an alternate factory // to override it. It is useful if you want to store custom // attributes per connection (authenticated bool flag, attributes, etc...) std::cout << "id: " << connectionState->getId() << std::endl; // The uri the client did connect to. std::cout << "Uri: " << msg->openInfo.uri << std::endl; std::cout << "Headers:" << std::endl; for (auto it : msg->openInfo.headers) { std::cout << it.first << ": " << it.second << std::endl; } } else if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Message) { // For an echo server, we just send back to the client whatever was received by the server // All connected clients are available in an std::set. See the broadcast cpp example. // Second parameter tells whether we are sending the message in binary or text mode. // Here we send it in the same mode as it was received. auto ws = webSocket.lock(); if (ws) { ws->send(msg->str, msg->binary); } } } ); } } ); auto res = server.listen(); if (!res.first) { // Error handling return 1; } // Per message deflate connection is enabled by default. It can be disabled // which might be helpful when running on low power devices such as a Rasbery Pi server.disablePerMessageDeflate(); // Run the server in the background. Server can be stoped by calling server.stop() server.start(); // Block until server.stop() is called. server.wait(); Client message callback setOnClientMessageCallback() installs one handler for all connections. Its WebSocket reference is valid for the duration of the callback. Use the connection setup callback above when a weak handle must outlive an individual callback. #include <ixwebsocket/IXWebSocketServer.h> ... // Run a server on localhost at a given port. // Bound host name, max connections and listen backlog can also be passed in as parameters. int port = 8008; std::string host("127.0.0.1"); // If you need this server to be accessible on a different machine, use "0.0.0.0" ix::WebSocketServer server(port, host); server.setOnClientMessageCallback([](std::shared_ptr<ix::ConnectionState> connectionState, ix::WebSocket & webSocket, const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr & msg) { // The ConnectionState object contains information about the connection, // at this point only the client ip address and the port. std::cout << "Remote ip: " << connectionState->getRemoteIp() << std::endl; if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Open) { std::cout << "New connection" << std::endl; // A connection state object is available, and has a default id // You can subclass ConnectionState and pass an alternate factory // to override it. It is useful if you want to store custom // attributes per connection (authenticated bool flag, attributes, etc...) std::cout << "id: " << connectionState->getId() << std::endl; // The uri the client did connect to. std::cout << "Uri: " << msg->openInfo.uri << std::endl; std::cout << "Headers:" << std::endl; for (auto it : msg->openInfo.headers) { std::cout << "\t" << it.first << ": " << it.second << std::endl; } } else if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Message) { // For an echo server, we just send back to the client whatever was received by the server // All connected clients are available in an std::set. See the broadcast cpp example. // Second parameter tells whether we are sending the message in binary or text mode. // Here we send it in the same mode as it was received. std::cout << "Received: " << msg->str << std::endl; webSocket.send(msg->str, msg->binary); } }); auto res = server.listen(); if (!res.first) { // Error handling return 1; } // Per message deflate connection is enabled by default. It can be disabled // which might be helpful when running on low power devices such as a Rasbery Pi server.disablePerMessageDeflate(); // Run the server in the background. Server can be stoped by calling server.stop() server.start(); // Block until server.stop() is called. server.wait(); Heartbeat You can configure an optional heartbeat / keep-alive for the WebSocket server. The heartbeat interval can be adjusted or disabled when constructing the WebSocketServer . Setting the interval to -1 disables the heartbeat feature; this is the default setting. The parameter you set will be applied to every WebSocket object that the server creates. To enable a 45 second heartbeat on a WebSocketServer : int pingIntervalSeconds = 45; ix::WebSocketServer server(port, host, backlog, maxConnections, handshakeTimeoutSecs, addressFamily, pingIntervalSeconds); Server log callback By default the server writes internal errors to stderr (and some info messages to stdout). Errors that happen before a connection is fully established — for example a failed TLS handshake when a client presents a bad certificate — cannot be reported through setOnClientMessageCallback , since no WebSocket object exists yet at that point. To capture those messages in your application logs, set a log callback. It applies to WebSocketServer as well as HttpServer . When a callback is set, messages are delivered to it instead of being written to stderr/stdout. server.setLogCallback([](ix::LogLevel level, const std::string& msg) { if (level == ix::LogLevel::Error) { myLogger.error(msg); } else { myLogger.info(msg); } }); HTTP client API Connection reuse Keep an ix::HttpClient instance alive to reuse its most recent HTTP/1.1 connection for sequential requests to the same scheme, hostname, and port. This also applies to requests queued through the asynchronous API and avoids repeating TCP/TLS setup. Only one idle connection is retained; requests remain serialized rather than pipelined. The client consumes the complete response before reusing a connection, including chunked trailers and same-origin redirect bodies. Connection: close in either request or response prevents retention. To close the connection after a request: auto args = client.createRequest(); args->extraHeaders["Connection"] = "close"; auto response = client.get(url, args); Calling setTLSOptions() or setProxyOptions() discards the cached connection. Configure them before issuing requests. Canceled, malformed, and incomplete transfers are closed. If an idle connection closes while a new request is starting, a bodyless GET or HEAD can be retried once before any response bytes arrive. Uploads and other methods are never automatically replayed after a transport failure; applications must decide whether retrying is appropriate. The built-in HttpServer still serves one ordinary HTTP request per connection and sends Connection: close . Reuse needs a server that supports persistent HTTP. Upgrading an authenticated HTTP connection to WebSocket webSocket.connect(httpClient, timeoutSecs) upgrades the HTTP client's idle connection in place. This supports servers that require HTTP authentication and the WebSocket upgrade on the same TCP/TLS connection: ix::HttpClient httpClient; // Configure TLS and proxy options on httpClient before the HTTP requests. auto args = httpClient.createRequest(); auto auth = httpClient.post("https://example.com/login", "credentials", args); if (auth->errorCode != ix::HttpErrorCode::Ok || auth->statusCode != 200) { // Handle authentication failure. return; } ix::WebSocket webSocket; webSocket.setUrl("wss://example.com/events"); webSocket.setExtraHeaders({{"Authorization", "Bearer " + auth->body}}); webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& message) { // Open runs on the connecting thread; messages run on the receiving thread. }); auto upgraded = webSocket.connect(httpClient, 5); if (!upgraded.success) { // No replacement connection or redirect is attempted. Authenticate again if needed. return; } webSocket.start(); // Receive on the connection that was just upgraded. // ... webSocket.stop(); The WebSocket must be stopped and closed, with a callback registered. Its ws:// or wss:// URL must match the HTTP connection's hostname, effective port, and TLS mode ( http to ws , https to wss ). The server must support persistent HTTP; a response with Connection: close leaves no connection available for handoff. An active HTTP request makes the upgrade fail immediately. An unavailable, stale, or mismatched connection also fails instead of silently opening a new one. Ownership moves to WebSocket , including TLS state and buffered input. Destroying HttpClient afterward leaves the WebSocket intact; later HTTP requests use a new connection. TLS and proxy settings are inherited from the HTTP client. Other WebSocket options, including extra headers, compression, subprotocols, and message limits, apply normally. Authentication headers and cookies are supplied explicitly with setExtraHeaders() ; they are not copied automatically from HTTP requests. Once the connection is handed off, automatic reconnection is disabled, including when the upgrade is rejected. To repeat connection-bound authentication, stop the WebSocket, authenticate through HTTP again, and repeat the handoff. Redirects and failed handshakes close the handed-off connection. The HTTP client is not retained. Call start() only after a successful handoff; on a closed WebSocket, start() remains the normal entry point for establishing a connection. Normal webSocket.start() continues to establish and upgrade a single connection without involving HttpClient . Making HTTP requests #include <ixwebsocket/IXHttpClient.h> ... // // Preparation // HttpClient httpClient; HttpRequestArgsPtr args = httpClient.createRequest(); // Custom headers can be set WebSocketHttpHeaders headers; headers["Foo"] = "bar"; args->extraHeaders = headers; // Timeout options args->connectTimeout = connectTimeout; args->transferTimeout = transferTimeout; // Redirect options args->followRedirects = followRedirects; args->maxRedirects = maxRedirects; // Misc args->compress = compress; // Enable gzip compression args->verbose = verbose; args->logger = [](const std::string& msg) { std::cout << msg; }; // // Synchronous Request // HttpResponsePtr out; std::string url = "https://www.google.com"; // HEAD request out = httpClient.head(url, args); // GET request out = httpClient.get(url, args); // POST request with parameters HttpParameters httpParameters; httpParameters["foo"] = "bar"; // HTTP form data can be passed in as well, for multi-part upload of files HttpFormDataParameters httpFormDataParameters; httpParameters["baz"] = "booz"; out = httpClient.post(url, httpParameters, httpFormDataParameters, args); // POST request with a body out = httpClient.post(url, std::string("foo=bar"), args); // PUT and PATCH are available too. // // Result // auto statusCode = response->statusCode; // Can be HttpErrorCode::Ok, HttpErrorCode::UrlMalformed, etc... auto errorCode = response->errorCode; // 200, 404, etc... auto responseHeaders = response->headers; // All the headers in a special case-insensitive unordered_map of (string, string) auto body = response->body; // All the bytes from the response as an std::string auto errorMsg = response->errorMsg; // Descriptive error message in case of failure auto uploadSize = response->uploadSize; // Byte count of uploaded data auto downloadSize = response->downloadSize; // Byte count of downloaded data // // Asynchronous Request // bool async = true; HttpClient httpClient(async); auto args = httpClient.createRequest(url, HttpClient::kGet); // If you define a chunk callback it will be called repeteadly with the // incoming data. This allows to process data on the go or write it to disk // instead of accumulating the data in memory. args.onChunkCallback = [](const std::string& data) { // process data }; // Push the request to a queue, bool ok = httpClient.performRequest(args, [](const HttpResponsePtr& response) { // This callback execute in a background thread. Make sure you uses appropriate protection such as mutex auto statusCode = response->statusCode; // acess results // response->body is empty if onChunkCallback was used } ); // ok will be false if your httpClient is not async // A request in progress can be cancelled by setting the cancel flag. It does nothing if the request already completed. args->cancel = true; performRequest() copies the request configuration when it is submitted. After it returns, reusing the arguments for another URL, body, or headers does not change earlier queued requests. Do not modify the configuration concurrently with the submission itself. Callbacks are copied, but objects they capture still need to remain valid when the callbacks run. The original args->cancel flag remains the cancellation handle, including while following redirects. Reusing an arguments object shares that flag across its submitted requests; use separate arguments objects for independently cancellable requests. HTTP connection reuse is not provided by this behavior. Automatic HTTP and WebSocket redirects retain caller-supplied Authorization and Cookie headers only while the scheme, hostname and port stay the same. Once a redirect changes origin, these headers remain removed for the rest of that redirect chain. The caller's original request arguments are preserved. Other custom headers are forwarded; applications should avoid putting credentials in those headers when following redirects to untrusted destinations. See this issue for links about uploading files with HTTP multipart. Uploading large files Use HttpRequestArgs::onUploadCallback to send a request body without loading the whole file into a string. Set bodySize to its known byte length; it is a 64-bit value, so uploads larger than 2 GiB are supported. The client sends a standard Content-Length request, using a reusable buffer of at most 64 KiB. #include <fstream> #include <ixwebsocket/IXHttpClient.h> #include <memory> #include <stdexcept> ix::HttpClient client; auto args = client.createRequest(); auto file = std::make_shared<std::ifstream>("large-file.bin", std::ios::binary | std::ios::ate); if (!*file || file->tellg() < 0) { throw std::runtime_error("Cannot open upload file"); } args->bodySize = static_cast<uint64_t>(static_cast<std::streamoff>(file->tellg())); args->extraHeaders["Content-Type"] = "application/octet-stream"; args->onUploadCallback = [file](uint64_t offset, char* buffer, size_t capacity) -> size_t { file->clear(); file->seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(offset)); file->read(buffer, static_cast<std::streamsize>(capacity)); return static_cast<size_t>(file->gcount()); }; auto response = client.put("https://example.com/upload", std::string(), args); The callback receives an absolute body offset and the available buffer capacity. Return the number of bytes written, at most that capacity. Short reads are allowed; a zero return before bodySize bytes, an invalid count, or an exception fails the request with HttpErrorCode::SendError . Set args->cancel to cancel an upload. Callbacks must return promptly for cancellation and transfer timeouts to take effect. Pass an empty string as the body when using the callback. It works with POST, PUT, PATCH, and methods enabled through setForceBody(true) , for synchronous requests and queued requests through performRequest . Keep the data source alive until completion; the shared pointer in this example also works for asynchronous requests. Redirects replay the body from offset zero, so the source must support rereading. Do not set Content-Length yourself or enable compressRequest for streamed uploads. To use Transfer-Encoding: chunked , see below. To upload a multipart body, the callback must supply its complete framing and a matching Content-Type ; the existing form-data helpers still assemble their bodies in memory. This API streams outgoing client data; the built-in HTTP server still buffers incoming request bodies. Chunked request uploads Set Transfer-Encoding: chunked to upload a body whose length is unknown, or when an endpoint requires chunked requests. With onUploadCallback , bodySize is ignored and returning zero finishes the body. Throw an exception on a source read error; it fails the request with HttpErrorCode::SendError . ix::HttpClient client; auto args = client.createRequest(); auto file = std::make_shared<std::ifstream>("upload.bin", std::ios::binary); if (!*file) { throw std::runtime_error("Cannot open upload file"); } args->extraHeaders["Transfer-Encoding"] = "chunked"; args->extraHeaders["Content-Type"] = "application/octet-stream"; args->onUploadCallback = [file](uint64_t offset, char* buffer, size_t capacity) -> size_t { file->clear(); file->seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(offset)); file->read(buffer, static_cast<std::streamsize>(capacity)); if (file->bad() || (file->fail() && !file->eof())) { throw std::runtime_error("Cannot read upload file"); } return static_cast<size_t>(file->gcount()); }; auto response = client.put("https://example.com/upload", std::string(), args); Include the same C++ headers as the file upload example above. The client supplies chunk framing and the terminating chunk, using data chunks of at most 64 KiB. You can also set this header with a regular string body. Do not combine it with Content-Length , request compression, or other transfer codings. Existing uploads continue to use Content-Length by default. Cancellation and redirect replay work as for fixed-length uploads; a 303 redirect switches to GET and drops the body. For asynchronous uploads, use HttpClient(true) and performRequest as usual. onChunkCallback receives response data; onResponseCallback runs once when the request completes. Each request finishes sending its body before reading its response; simultaneous request and response streaming is not supported. The built-in HttpServer currently accepts Content-Length request bodies and buffers them in memory; it does not decode chunked request bodies. Use a server that supports chunked requests as the upload endpoint. HTTP server API #include <ixwebsocket/IXHttpServer.h> ix::HttpServer server(port, hostname); server.setDocumentRoot("www"); auto res = server.listen(); if (!res.first) { std::cerr << res.second << std::endl; return 1; } server.start(); server.wait(); The built-in static file handler serves the current directory by default. Call setDocumentRoot(path) before starting the server to select a relative or absolute directory. An empty path selects the current directory. Relative paths are resolved against the process working directory, and requests for / serve index.html . This setting applies to the built-in handler; custom connection callbacks continue to handle their own responses. The command-line server provides the same option: ws httpd --port 8008 --document-root www If you want to handle how requests are processed, implement the setOnConnectionCallback callback, which takes an HttpRequestPtr as input, and returns an HttpResponsePtr. You can look at HttpServer::setDefaultConnectionCallback for a slightly more advanced callback example. setOnConnectionCallback( [this](HttpRequestPtr request, std::shared_ptr<ConnectionState> connectionState) -> HttpResponsePtr { // Build a string for the response std::stringstream ss; ss << connectionState->getRemoteIp(); << " " << request->method << " " << request->uri; std::string content = ss.str(); return std::make_shared<HttpResponse>(200, "OK", HttpErrorCode::Ok, WebSocketHttpHeaders(), content); } TLS support and configuration To leverage TLS features, the library must be compiled with the option USE_TLS=1 . If you are using OpenSSL, try to be on a version higher than 1.1.x as there there are thread safety problems with 1.0.x. Then, secure sockets are automatically used when connecting to a wss://* url. Additional TLS options can be configured by passing a ix::SocketTLSOptions instance to the setTLSOptions on ix::WebSocket (or ix::WebSocketServer or ix::HttpServer ) A TLS-enabled build still creates a plain server listener by default. Enable TLS on the listener before calling listen() : ix::SocketTLSOptions serverTLS; serverTLS.tls = true; serverTLS.certFile = "path/to/server-cert.pem"; serverTLS.keyFile = "path/to/server-key.pem"; server.setTLSOptions(serverTLS); Clients select TLS with a wss:// URL. For a local server signed by a private CA, configure the matching trust bundle before starting the client: ix::SocketTLSOptions clientTLS; clientTLS.caFile = "path/to/ca.pem"; webSocket.setTLSOptions(clientTLS); webSocket.setUrl("wss://localhost:8008"); Specifying certFile and keyFile configures the certificate that will be used to communicate with TLS peers. On a client, this is only necessary for connecting to servers that require a client certificate. With OpenSSL, mbedTLS, and Network.framework, certFile and keyFile can each contain either a file path or the PEM contents directly, just like caFile : ix::SocketTLSOptions options; options.certFile = certificateChainPEM; // Leaf certificate first, then intermediates. options.keyFile = privateKeyPEM; // Matching, unencrypted PEM private key. options.caFile = trustedRootsPEM; // Or a CA file path / "SYSTEM". webSocket.setTLSOptions(options); The same options work for TLS servers ( options.tls = true ). File paths and in-memory contents can be mixed; no temporary credential files are created. Unencrypted PKCS#8, RSA, and EC PEM keys are supported. Encrypted private keys have no password API and are not supported. getDescription() redacts in-memory PEM contents. SecureTransport does not support in-memory local credentials; use Network.framework on macOS for this feature. On a server, this is necessary for TLS support. Specifying caFile configures the trusted roots bundle file (in PEM format) that will be used to verify peer certificates. - The special value of SYSTEM (the default) indicates that the system-configured trust bundle should be used; this is generally what you want when connecting to any publicly exposed API/server. - The special value of NONE can be used to disable peer verification; this is only recommended to rule out certificate verification when testing connectivity. - If the value contain the special value -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- , the value will be read from memory, and not from a file. This is convenient on platforms like Android where reading / writing to the file system can be challenging without proper permissions, or without knowing the location of a temp directory. The Mbed TLS backend currently supports caFile = "SYSTEM" only on Windows. On other platforms, including macOS, set caFile explicitly to the path of a trusted PEM CA bundle or its PEM contents, including for publicly trusted servers. Otherwise the connection fails with an error explaining the missing configuration. Use a bundle containing a trusted root for the server's certificate chain; keep hostname and certificate verification enabled. For a client, specifying caFile can be used if connecting to a server that uses a self-signed cert, or when using a custom CA in an internal environment. For a server, specifying caFile implies that: 1. You require clients to present a certificate 1. It must be signed by one of the trusted roots in the file By default, a destination's hostname is always validated against the certificate that it presents. To accept certificates with any hostname, set ix::SocketTLSOptions::disable_hostname_validation to true . TLS key logging (OpenSSL) With OpenSSL 1.1.1 or newer, set keyLogFile in your TLS options before connecting or starting a TLS server: ix::SocketTLSOptions options; options.keyLogFile = "tls.keys"; webSocket.setTLSOptions(options); The file contains TLS session secrets in NSS key-log format, which tools such as Wireshark can use to decrypt captured traffic. An empty keyLogFile disables this logging. Connections append to the file, including across reconnections; multiple connections may share a destination. A connection fails if the file cannot be opened. Other TLS backends reject this option explicitly. The ws TLS commands accept --keylog-file and the SSLKEYLOGFILE environment variable. An explicit command-line option takes precedence: ws connect wss://example.com/ws --keylog-file tls.keys SSLKEYLOGFILE=tls.keys ws connect wss://example.com/ws The library API uses keyLogFile explicitly; environment-variable handling is provided by the CLI. Network.framework backend on macOS Build with USE_NETWORK_FRAMEWORK=ON to use native TLS for wss:// and https:// clients and TLS-enabled WebSocket/HTTP servers. Network.framework handles connection setup, DNS, and TCP. Application HTTP and WebSocket handling stays in IXWebSocket. TLS 1.2 is the minimum; TLS 1.3 is negotiated when supported by the peer. The existing SocketTLSOptions fields apply: certFile and keyFile accept a PEM certificate chain (leaf first) and matching, unencrypted PEM private key. Both are required for a TLS server and optional for a client presenting a certificate. Credentials are imported in memory, without installing them in a keychain. caFile = "SYSTEM" uses Apple's trust evaluation and configured system trust. A PEM CA file or in-memory PEM bundle instead restricts trust to those anchors. caFile = "NONE" disables peer verification. On a server this also disables the requirement for a client certificate. Other CA settings require client authentication, matching the existing server options. disable_hostname_validation skips the client's hostname check while retaining certificate trust evaluation. IP literals are checked against IP SAN entries. Custom ciphers strings are currently rejected; leave ciphers at DEFAULT . The native server uses a Network.framework listener. createSocket cannot adopt an existing BSD descriptor for TLS with this backend. The listener requires a numeric bind address and uses the framework's TCP listen queue rather than the BSD backlog setting. Pending connections are bounded by maxConnections . Server TLS handshakes have a ten-second limit and are interrupted when the server stops. Client connection timeouts use the caller's cancellation callback, including HTTP/WebSocket timeouts. SOCKS5 client proxies Configure an outbound SOCKS5 proxy before connecting a WebSocket or issuing HTTP requests. The same options apply to HTTP, HTTPS, WS, and WSS: ix::ProxyOptions proxy; proxy.host = "127.0.0.1"; proxy.port = 1080; // default proxy.dnsMode = ix::ProxyOptions::DnsMode::Remote; // default: proxy resolves the destination webSocket.setProxyOptions(proxy); httpClient.setProxyOptions(proxy); Use DnsMode::Local to resolve the destination locally and send an IPv4 or IPv6 address to the proxy. Numeric destinations are always sent as numeric addresses. The proxy's own hostname is resolved locally in both modes. TLS continues to use the original destination hostname for SNI and certificate verification. Set both proxy.username and proxy.password to offer SOCKS username/password authentication as well as the unauthenticated method. Each credential must contain 1–255 bytes. Proxy authentication takes place before the destination TLS handshake. An empty proxy host disables this proxy configuration; call setProxyOptions({}) to clear it. Configure options before use; WebSocket reconnections use the current configuration. Proxy negotiation shares the existing connection timeout and cancellation mechanism, and failures do not fall back to a direct connection. SOCKS5 CONNECT is supported for plain sockets, OpenSSL/LibreSSL, Mbed TLS, and SecureTransport. SOCKS4 and HTTP CONNECT proxies are not implemented. The native Network.framework TLS backend currently returns an explicit unsupported-proxy error. Its native SOCKS API failed routing and fragmented-reply checks during implementation, so it is not enabled by this feature.

docs.text: To use the network system on Windows, you need to initialize it once with WSAStartup() and clean it up with WSACleanup() . We have helpers for that which you can use, see below. This init would typically take place in your main function. On every platform, ix::uninitNetSystem() also releases process-global TLS state (mbedTLS PSA crypto, with mbedTLS >= 3.6), so call it only after all sockets are closed. #include <ixwebsocket/IXNetSystem.h> int main() { ix::initNetSystem(); ... ix::uninitNetSystem(); return 0; }

docs.text: #include <ixwebsocket/IXWebSocket.h> ... // Our websocket object ix::WebSocket webSocket; std::string url("ws://localhost:8080/"); webSocket.setUrl(url); // Optional heart beat, sent every 45 seconds when there is not any traffic // to make sure that load balancers do not kill an idle connection. webSocket.setPingInterval(45); // Per message deflate connection is not enabled by default. You can tweak its parameters, enable or disable it with webSocket.enablePerMessageDeflate(); webSocket.disablePerMessageDeflate(); // Setup a callback to be fired when a message or an event (open, close, error) is received webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Message) { std::cout << msg->str << std::endl; } } ); // Now that our callback is setup, we can start our background thread and receive messages webSocket.start(); // Send a message to the server (default to TEXT mode) webSocket.send("hello world"); // The message can be sent in BINARY mode (useful if you send MsgPack data for example) webSocket.sendBinary("some serialized binary data"); // ... finally ... // Stop the connection webSocket.stop()

docs.text: WebSocketSendInfo result = websocket.send("foo") will send a message. If the connection was closed, sending will fail, and the success field of the result object will be set to false. There could also be a compression error in which case the compressError field will be set to true. The payloadSize field and wireSize fields will tell you respectively how much bytes the message weight, and how many bytes were sent on the wire (potentially compressed + counting the message header (a few bytes). There is an optional progress callback that can be passed in as the second argument. If a message is large it will be fragmented into chunks which will be sent independantly. Everytime the we can write a fragment into the OS network cache, the callback will be invoked. If a user wants to cancel a slow send, false should be returned from within the callback. Here is an example code snippet copied from the ws send sub-command. Each fragment weights 32K, so the total integer is the wireSize divided by 32K. As an example if you are sending 32M of data, uncompressed, total will be 1000. current will be set to 0 for the first fragment, then 1, 2 etc... auto result = _webSocket.sendBinary(serializedMsg, [this, throttle](int current, int total) -> bool { ix::logInfo("ws_send: Step {} out of {}", current + 1, total); if (throttle) { std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli> duration(10); std::this_thread::sleep_for(duration); } return _connected; }); The send() and sendText() methods check that the string contains only valid UTF-8 characters. If you know that the string is a valid UTF-8 string you can skip that step and use the sendUtf8Text method instead. With the IXWebSocketSendData overloads of sendUtf8Text and sendBinary it is possible to not only send std::string but also std::vector<char> , std::vector<uint8_t> and char* . std::vector<uint8_t> data({1, 2, 3, 4}); auto result = webSocket.sendBinary(data); const char* text = "Hello World!"; result = webSocket.sendUtf8Text(IXWebSocketSendData(text, strlen(text)));
docs.title: Sending messages

docs.text: Incoming messages are unlimited by default. Set a limit in bytes before connecting or starting the server: webSocket.setMaxMessageSize(1024 * 1024); // Client: 1 MiB per incoming message. server.setMaxMessageSize(1024 * 1024); // Server: default for new connections. getMaxMessageSize() returns the configured limit; setMaxMessageSize(0) restores unlimited messages. Client settings apply on the next connection, including reconnections. Server settings also apply to WebSocket upgrades through HttpServer . The limit covers the combined payload of all fragments, both before and after per-message decompression. Control frames do not count toward the limit. Oversized messages close the connection with code 1009 (Message Too Big), without delivering that message. Frame lengths are checked before buffering their payload; decompression stops before appending output beyond the limit. This is a per-message limit, rather than a total process memory budget. Choose it alongside your connection limit and application buffering requirements. The echo server exposes the same setting: ws echo_server --port 8080 --max-message-size 1048576

docs.text: getReadyState() returns the state of the connection. There are 4 possible states. ReadyState::Connecting - The connection is not yet open. ReadyState::Open - The connection is open and ready to communicate. ReadyState::Closing - The connection is in the process of closing. ReadyState::Closed - The connection is closed or could not be opened.

docs.text: The onMessage event will be fired when the connection is opened or closed. This is similar to the JavaScript browser API , which has open and close events notification that can be registered with the browser addEventListener . webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Open) { std::cout << "send greetings" << std::endl; // Headers can be inspected (pairs of string/string) std::cout << "Handshake Headers:" << std::endl; for (auto it : msg->headers) { std::cout << it.first << ": " << it.second << std::endl; } } else if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Close) { std::cout << "disconnected" << std::endl; // The server can send an explicit code and reason for closing. // This data can be accessed through the closeInfo object. std::cout << msg->closeInfo.code << std::endl; std::cout << msg->closeInfo.reason << std::endl; } } );

docs.text: A message will be fired when there is an error with the connection. The message type will be ix::WebSocketMessageType::Error . Multiple fields will be available on the event to describe the error. When a server rejects the WebSocket handshake, msg->errorInfo.headers contains the HTTP response headers, such as Retry-After or custom authentication headers. Header names are case insensitive. Errors without response headers leave this map empty. webSocket.setOnMessageCallback([](const ix::WebSocketMessagePtr& msg) { if (msg->type == ix::WebSocketMessageType::Error) { std::stringstream ss; ss << "Error: " << msg->errorInfo.reason << std::endl; ss << "#retries: " << msg->errorInfo.retries << std::endl; ss << "Wait time(ms): " << msg->errorInfo.wait_time << std::endl; ss << "HTTP Status: " << msg->errorInfo.http_status << std::endl; std::cout << ss.str() << std::endl; } } );
